answer:
Normalize embeddings and form a cosine-similarity matrix divided by temperature. CLIP uses cross-view matrices in both directions; SimCLR uses all 2N embeddings and excludes only each example’s self-match. The paired alternate view remains the positive. In-batch negatives can include semantically valid matches, so a multi-positive objective may be needed in real retrieval data.

**Mathematical and practical explanation.** For paired embeddings, $L_i=-\log\frac{e^{s_{i,i^+}/\tau}}{\sum_{j\in C(i)}e^{s_{ij}/\tau}}$. Temperature controls concentration and gradient scale. Correct candidate sets matter: exclude self-comparisons for SimCLR while preserving the alternate-view positive, and use symmetric image-to-text/text-to-image objectives for CLIP-style training. [3](https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.00020)

For the implementation or system context discussed above, see [1](https://lilianweng.github.io/posts/2021-05-31-contrastive/) and [2](https://gombru.github.io/2018/05/23/cross_entropy_loss/).
